pages.name: Where i lands
pages.text: Take the matrix `[2 −1; 1 1]`. The arrow i is `(1, 0)`, so it takes 1 lot of column 1 and none of column 2. So i lands on column 1, `(2, 1)`, and the grid follows it.

pages.name: Where j lands
pages.why: Arrow j is `(0, 1)`. So it takes no lots of column 1 and 1 lot of column 2. Column 2 runs down through −1 and 1, so j lands on `(−1, 1)`.

pages.name: Every point follows
pages.text: The point `(1, 2)` is 1 lot of i plus 2 lots of j. So it lands on 1 lot of `(2, 1)` plus 2 lots of `(−1, 1)`, which is `(0, 3)`. Each step along a grid line adds the same column. So the lines stay straight and evenly spaced, unless the move squashes them flat. The origin is no lots of anything, so it never moves.

pages.name: Where (3, 1) lands
pages.why: `(3, 1)` is 3 lots of i plus 1 lot of j. So it lands on 3 lots of `(2, 1)` plus 1 lot of `(−1, 1)`. That is `(6, 3)` plus `(−1, 1)`, which is `(5, 4)`.

pages.name: Named moves
pages.text: The mirror `[−1 0; 0 1]` sends i to `(−1, 0)` and keeps j. So the F faces the other way. A [[shear]] such as `[1 1; 0 1]` keeps i and slides j to `(1, 1)`. Every named move is just two landing spots.

pages.task: Here i lands on `(3, 1)` and j on `(0, 2)`. Which matrix makes this move?
pages.why: Arrow i lands on `(3, 1)`, so 3 and 1 run down column 1. Arrow j lands on `(0, 2)`, so 0 and 2 run down column 2. That gives `[3 0; 1 2]`.

pages.name: A turn
pages.text: A turn anticlockwise through θ sends i to `(cos θ, sin θ)`, on the unit circle. A quarter turn sends any arrow `(a, b)` to `(−b, a)`. Arrow j starts a quarter turn ahead of i, so it lands on `(−sin θ, cos θ)`. Turned 30°, i lands on `(0.87, 0.5)` and j on `(−0.5, 0.87)`.

pages.name: Turn a point
pages.task: Where does `(2, 1)` land under the quarter turn `[0 −1; 1 0]`?
pages.why: `(2, 1)` lands on 2 lots of `(0, 1)` plus 1 lot of `(−1, 0)`. That is `(−1, 2)`. A quarter turn sends `(a, b)` to `(−b, a)`, which agrees. It is the same quarter turn as multiplying by j in complex numbers.

pages.name: What no matrix does
pages.task: Which move can no 2 by 2 matrix make?
pages.why: A matrix times `(0, 0)` is no lots of anything, so the origin stays put. A slide would move the origin 3 squares right. So no 2 by 2 matrix can make it.
